full_judgment: 6. Mr A R Yusuf, the learned Counsel appearing with Advocate Syed Mahmudul Ahsan for respondent Nos. 2 to 6, submits that since the register of members of the Company shows the respondent Nos. 2 to 7 in place of the petitioner as share-holders of the company there is a valid presumption under section 45 of the Companies Act, 1994 that the transfer of the said 10,000 shares in favour of the respondent Nos. 2 to 7 was valid. With regard to affixing of requisite stamps on the instrument of transfer, which is admittedly not done, the learned Advocate submits that non-payment of such stamp duty at the relevant time of transfer could not render the transfer invalid as the instrument of transfer in this case can be affixed with requisite stamps even now as there is no time limit in this regard. Mr Yusuf referred to and relied on-the decision reported in 43 DLR 329 of this Court in this connection.
